design.summary: Build four small changes and drop two parts of the synthesis. (1) R1: keep every non-rule path 'pending' (fail-closed). Add a script verb `workspace review-return --keep/--exclude PATH...` that records decisions, validates them against the existing protected-path rules and names any offending path. Make `plan-return` and the blocked `return` list the undecided paths with the exact command. Make a re-run of `plan-return` keep decisions already recorded for the same path. Reword the 'left uncommitted' line. (2) R2: replace the generic 'not a Git merge or commit' packet sentence with a script-derived route sentence built from workspace.md's start_clean. Print a script-derived rollback at release-plan and release-check, and have the verb report the expected return kind. Correct the synthesis's rollback anchor: it must be workspace.md (source_head, or baseline_commit plus the run branch), not 'the head the receipt records'. (3) F1: put the action and the paths on the first line of the knowledge-close refusal, the pending-dispositions refusal and the backchain-check 'not JSON' message, and name the allowed values in 'invalid status'. (4) N1: create run/notes/ in `emit`. Dropped: R1(a), default 'keep' by declared step-plan paths (it would not have unblocked either run, and a wrong default ships files), and R1(c), a release-check script gate (the named-path refusal makes the dry run cheap, and the gate belongs with R3).
design.for_against: FOR. S-4 and S-5 name hand-edited script files and directory creation as script work. In both runs the first real return blocked with no path (checkers events 397-414: 7 calls, blanket `sed -i`; battleship events 471-493: 8 calls, invented status 'reviewed'). The wrong rollback landed in the durable knowledge home that later runs inherit (S-11). Every change is small and generic, adds no state key, and needs no migration. The verb keeps the owner's 'supply judgment, not shell glue' split. AGAINST. Time saved is small (about 4-5 calls, 20-35 s per run), so the value is fidelity, not speed. The verb is new surface (one subparser and one function). Carry-over of decisions across `plan-return` is a policy choice: a path kept earlier stays kept even if its content later changes. The default-keep idea was refused on evidence: declared step-plan paths cover 6 of 7 (battleship) and 5 of 7 (checkers) pending rows, so a block would remain in both runs. The undeclared rows are README.md and test/system.test.js, which other stages legitimately write (candidate D2). commit_leftovers also commits every non-protected stray file before the plan is made, so a default keep would turn any scratch file into shipped output.

per_candidate.change: Keep the default 'pending' for every path no rule decides. Add `review_return` (script verb `workspace review-return --keep/--exclude`). Make the pending refusal a `PendingDispositions` error carrying the paths. Print the tally, the pending paths and the exact verb from `plan-return`. Carry recorded dispositions across `plan_return`. Fix the leftover wording. Drop (a) default-keep by declared paths: partial in both runs, and a wrong default 'keep' ships an unwanted file. Drop (c), the release-check gate: it needs a new complete-check kind for one stage, so coordinate with candidate R3 and do not build it here. The synthesis's claim that status needs editing is already corrected: only dispositions matter, and 'ready' is just the script's own label.

Script-derived route sentence in every worktree packet (replacing the misleading generic sentence). Script-derived rollback lines at release-plan and release-check. Expected return kind printed by `review-return` once nothing is pending, from a predicate shared with `execute_return`. One sentence in each of the release-plan and release-check duties. Drop the script-checked plan-vs-route comparison (a model judgement grounded in script text). Fix the synthesis: the receipt's source_before.head is the PREVIOUS result in a follow-up receipt, so the anchor is workspace.md. Do not use the receipt's expected_source.working_tree tree: it is unreferenced and `git gc --prune=now` pruned it (measured) when a committed path was excluded.

Scope to the refusals the two runs hit. Knowledge-close missing files: first line carries 'Before <stage> is done, write: <relative paths>' and the absolute `- /path` lines stay, since route tests parse them. Pending dispositions: first line has the count, the first paths and the verb name; line 2 has the exact command. 'invalid status': name 'pending' or 'ready'. backchain-check 'not JSON': add that the candidate is the plan graph JSON, with a resolved path to prompts/generator.v1.md. Out of scope: credential-screen text (X1), Improve until-loop JSON errors (Improve group), K1's packet file list. `evidence_refs` is already first-line actionable.

Replace `_fail('return plan has unresolved path dispositions')` with a raise of PendingDispositions. Add the offending path to the protected-runtime, caller-excluded and knowledge-exclude refusals. Add the allowed values ('pending' or 'ready') to the invalid-status refusal.

Read the plan. Refuse a stale candidate, naming 'run plan-return again; your decisions are kept'. Reject a path that is not a plan row, or one named in both --keep and --exclude, listing the undecided paths. Apply decisions: an exact path overrides; a directory argument applies only to still-pending rows beneath it. ROLLBACK RECIPES (R2). (a) Drop `git revert --no-edit <source_head>..HEAD`. I reproduced it failing on a run branch that contains an integrate merge: 'commit ... is a merge but no -m option was given', after a partial revert that needs `git revert --abort`. `-m 1` cannot be applied to a mixed range. Use `git restore --source=<source_head> --staged --worktree :/` followed by a commit instead. I verified it leaves a tree identical to the base and removes added files. Alternatively keep only `reset --keep` and describe revert in prose. (b) Add 'while <source_branch> is checked out' to the `reset --keep` precondition. `reset --keep` moves whatever branch is current. (c) Run both sides of the working-tree pipeline with `git -C <source_repo>`: `git -C <source_repo> diff --binary <baseline_commit> <branch> -- <kept paths> | git -C <source_repo> apply -R`. I verified this restores the source after `git worktree remove`. It also keeps the worktree path out of release-plan.md, which is durable knowledge that later runs inherit (S-11). Tell the model to write the rollback with SHAs, branch names and repo-relative commands, not the run's absolute paths.

TEST PLACEMENT. test/shiploop-workspace.test.py measures 140.3 s in suite_catalog._DURATION_SECONDS, above QUICK_MAX_SECONDS=120. Register it in test/suite_catalog.py with a measured duration (none invented), and set GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 and GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null for its real-git cases and the `sh` runs of the printed recipes. In existing suites, change only the pinned wording: the 'Review all keep/exclude dispositions' assertion, rehydration for notes/, knowledge and backchain-check for the first lines.

STALE PLAN AT `return` (F1 scope). The new release-check duty tells the model to correct release-plan.md when the rollback does not match. ShipLoop commits the knowledge home after every accepted stage that changed it (navigator knowledge.commit, message 'after release-check'). That commit changes the candidate head, so the plan made at release-check is stale at `release`. The refusal 'return plan is stale because candidate state changed' names no remedy. Add it to the F1 set: 'run plan-return again; decisions already recorded are kept'. Also make the release-check duty say explicitly to run `plan-return` and `review-return` there and to re-run `plan-return` after correcting release-plan.md. Nothing today tells a model to run them at release-check, so 'compare with the route review-return reports' has no input.

ONE CARRY-OVER IMPLEMENTATION (S-12). follow_up_knowledge_return already carries reviewed dispositions with its own loop after calling plan_return. Move that loop into the new shared helper and delete it there. Leaving both makes two code paths for one mechanism. Also give `_expected_return` the follow-up case (prior receipt kind) and the no-change case, or the 'expected matches actual' parity test cannot hold after a first return.

CARRY-OVER SEMANTICS. Rows carry no content digest, so define 'unchanged path' as the same path and say so in workspace-lifecycle.md. Today it says 'Changed candidates require a fresh plan' and 'The new plan still reviews every path'; both need rewording. Print the carried decisions in plan-return's tally, at least the model-decided excludes by name. Otherwise a cleared-context model cannot see that README.md was excluded earlier and silently under-delivers. Do not carry a decision for a path commit_leftovers skipped as credential-like; leave it pending so the skipped notice forces a fresh decision. Take the workspace lock in plan_return (the lock is reentrant, so follow_up_knowledge_return still works), because a writer verb now exists beside it.

TENET AND UNKNOWN HANDLING. (a) When workspace.md cannot be read, print one line such as 'return route unknown: workspace.md unreadable (<error>)'. Do not omit the route silently; unmeasured is unknown. (b) Do not repeat the route sentence inside the release-plan and release-check rollback lines of a packet that already carries it. (c) End the review-return output with the exact next command: the `return` command when nothing is pending, otherwise the review template. A cleared context needs it. (d) Say 'update the grounding sentences' rather than 'size-neutral'. The new template and route sentence are longer than the two sentences they replace. The full packet file is not size-bounded, and the status-block window is unaffected.

design.summary: Build all four, each smaller than proposed. U1 (the only structural change): one optional result key `unverified` on a done product-acceptance result, a list of {outcome, reason, check, owner, due_stage}. ShipLoop REFUSES only mechanical faults at the CLI gate (key missing, malformed entry, the unedited template row, due_stage not a later stage); it only RECORDS what it cannot judge (whether the list is complete, whether [] is true, assumption coverage, headline wording); it PRINTS the list and the plan's still-open assumptions at product-acceptance and handoff and renders it in report.html. No new state key; the key is shape-checked in _canonical_result (absence loads) and required only in a new submit-time gate, the assumptions pattern. Case end-state mapping: an `unverified` entry is the recorded 'unachievable / not yet due' state; 'validated another way' stays a script-run check. The shared CASE_END_STATES is left unchanged on purpose (its 'report blocked' route is wrong for an outer open item under S-14 and for the inner stages, which cannot continue past a failing recorded command); product-acceptance gets its own three-state sentence in DUTIES. I2: the Improve parent packet gets the stage's Goal and Done-when through _goal_lines (reviewer side) plus one sentence in _improve_line; no producer Checked-by change (head window). K1: one stage_files() union, two alias entries deleted. W1: five wording fixes (discovery no-suite, research/intake vs S-14, release guard scoped to plan review, integrate chain/commit lines, 'independent'); (f) is folded into U1. I built this in a scratch copy (/private/tmp/g3/proto2, a copy of the b1008a worktree at abc47622 plus the changes and patched tests; no repo file was edited). Result: all 60 ShipLoop hermetic test files pass except those that fail identically on a pristine copy (chain, chain-async, chain-lifecycle, chain-planning-context, cross-run: 23 failures on both; one status-display test) and one guidance test that needs docs/experiments, which my copy excluded. The seven patched test files fail on the pristine copy for the reasons listed in fail_first_tests. Measured head (dry run, END of the status block, limit 8000): product-acceptance 5973 to 6347, Improve parent packets 4529 to 4876 (inline) and 4758 to 5105 (ask-agent), every other stage within 2 characters; the step-plan head is untouched.
design.for_against: For: both runs ignored the stage row's own 'pending with its owner and due stage' and put an 'all verified' headline over a prose limitation (checkers results/nav-6e9289db headline 'live server meets every request sentence' with 'Limitation: ... not driven in a real browser'; battleship results/nav-c6fbc982 'all request outcomes verified; UI clicks only statically', notes/acceptance.md 'pending, optional, no authorized browser used'); S-14 has required a recorded open item since 2026-09-27 and the 2026-10-04 'a13' route (test/shiploop_e2e/LEARNINGS.md) was deliberately text-only with no field, so the content (owner, due stage, what they report) has nowhere to live; the gate is the same class as the plan's assumption list (required at submit, optional on load); the test blast radius is three helper defaults plus new cases. Against: a model can write [] or perfunctory text and the script cannot tell; n=2 on one model; product-acceptance was a pass-through stage (docs/lifecycle-review-2026-10-07.md: 0.4 min) and now needs one more field; it reverses the a13 'text only' choice for this one stage. Why smaller than the synthesis: no refusal keyed on prose, headline words or assumption ids (KISS over adversarial guards), no producer Checked-by edit (head window), no change to the owner's shared CASE_END_STATES, reportable-only items (script-run baseline, return-plan status, notes/ directory, refusal first lines) left to the other groups. The 5-field entry adds `check` to the synthesis's 4 because S-14's open item is 'who must do what and what they should report'; drop it if the second run shows it is filled perfunctorily.

design.summary: Build B1 as proposed; build BC1 smaller than the candidate. B1: `init` (and the `workspace start` precheck) resolves the Improve card from the installed plugin when `--improve-skill` is absent, through one helper that reuses the plugin-skills-dir definition already used for the Backchain and Until Loop resources. It records the resolved path in the existing `improve_skill` key, so there is no new flag, no new state key, no migration, and an explicit `--improve-skill` still wins. When nothing resolves, a stage run keeps today's lazy bind but its packet prints a marked blank and an always-true sentence, never a fake path. A `none` run is refused only when no card is given and none is found. Prototype: 0 of 574 dry-run packets print the placeholder, against 106 before. BC1: say in the plan packet that the whole Backchain child is optional (the documented owner position) and that the dependency audit is not, and make the failure message of the printed `backchain-check` name the JSON graph shape and the Backchain section that defines it. The route is recorded as a sentence in the existing `summary`. Do not add a structured `backchain` result field now: a prototype shows it would break the plan fixtures of at least 9 test files and add a gate, a Checked-by clause, a template key and docs, for observability the Run Review can already derive from files.
design.for_against: B1 FOR: the placeholder is `/absolute/path/to/selected/improve/SKILL.md` in `_first_callback_lines` and `_render_improve`. Both Sonnet runs made the model hunt for the path by hand: battleship events 60-67 build `IMP=.../skills/improve/SKILL.md; ls $IMP` from the CLI path, and checkers event 61 does the same with `IC=`. design.summary:
Build H1 as one harness-only change, which is the long-deferred item M1 in docs/shiploop-callback-typos-plan-2026-10-04.md. Do not build the whole list in the candidate text. metrics.collect() should feed Claude tool_use and tool_result blocks through the single classifier the Grok tool_call path already uses (glue_reasons, tmp_writes, failure_line, stage tool calls, asked-person). The existing shapes are reused: model_glue, shiploop_failures, tmp_writes, stages[].tool_calls and the Codex per-stage context map {calls, peak, peakPct}. Only a few things are new.

Three details matter:
- Claude commands are multi-line shell with `RUN=...` assignments, so paths are expanded per command first (`expand_variables`).
- Refusals mostly sit behind exit 0 because the model pipes the CLI through head, grep or sed. They are detected by their line-anchored text, not by the exit code.
- `ShipLoop workspace blocked:` is a third refusal prefix that REFUSAL_LINE does not cover.

New record-only block `tool_use`:
- `calls`, `by_tool`, `result_chars`.
- `scratch_scripts`: files the model wrote that are invoked and either live under scratch/ or wrap the CLI.
- `packets`: `on_disk`, `printed`, `read`.

Two tiny host-independent fixes: `script_verifications.not_green` and `improve_reviews.identical`.

Dropped:
- No Claude compaction counter. No recorded stream has a compaction event, and the only context shrinks in 15 runs are session starts.
- No Claude truncated_outputs, knowledge_reads or cancelled_tool_calls.
- No exporter edits. The unmodified exporter already consumes the new fields: I ran export.py on a copy of the Battleship run with an edited metrics.json and got refusals 5, glue 1, per-stage context, and the facts.md lines.

A prototype on all 15 recorded Claude runs reproduced every lens figure that was hand-mined from events.jsonl.
design.for_against:
FOR:
- Every round-1 lens hand-mined events.jsonl for the same facts, because metrics.py CLAUDE_BLIND and CLAUDE_TOOL_BLOCKS leave stage_tool_calls, shiploop_failures, model_glue and tmp_writes unmeasured. LEARNINGS.md item 7 already admitted "the failure metric is blind for Claude" and planned M1.
- The prototype reproduces the hand figures exactly. Battleship: 120 tool calls (115 Bash, 4 Read, 1 Edit); 222,269 result chars; 5 refusals; 44 packet files of 1,707,162 B on disk; 4 Read calls (2 whole, 28,595 and 21,636 chars); 23 shell commands naming packets/ (64,249 chars); sub.sh run 30 times. Checkers: 209,381 chars, 45 files of 1,737,466 B.
- It surfaces a pattern: 14 of 15 recorded Claude runs wrote at least one invoked helper script that wraps the CLI. model_glue alone shows 0 to 3 because writes into run/scratch, inbox and notes are MODEL_INPUT.
- Live progress.py picks it up too, since it calls collect() on each poll.
- It serves SPEC S-1, S-2, S-4, S-5 and S-7 evidence. It is record-only: no state key, no packet text, no engine file.

AGAINST:
- Five existing tests pin "Claude is blind" and must flip.
- shared_tmp_writes now includes Claude runs. That is intended: r1 Battleship wrote the shared /tmp/bs.pid.
- Counts are heuristic lower bounds. Variable expansion is line-leading assignments only, and a wrapper hides its verb.
- A larger parser is not worth it. The compaction proxy, truncated_outputs, knowledge_reads, tool-error counts, Write-tool glue and next-id extraction counts were all considered and dropped (see per_candidate).
